Evidence: Twenty Homes campaign, private property offer, community trades
#Aletheia #Housing #Canberra

Jonny Warren's 20 Homes campaign works to secure safe, secure housing for vulnerable Canberra families before Christmas.

With hundreds of public housing properties vacant across the ACT, grassroots organizers like Jonny Warren and Adam Mumford turned to private donors and trades to bypass bureaucratic delays and house vulnerable families.

Stated Claim / Post Context:
Canberra tradies and businesses urged to help get a homeless family into a house by Christmas

"This is the moment we've been working towards," Twenty Homes founder Jonny Warren said.

Actual Article Body:

Jonny Warren's ambitious project to help Canberra's homeless before Christmas is underway, and the local real estate agent is euphoric.

Login or signup to continue reading

"This is the moment we've been working towards," he said.

Mr Warren's 20 Homes campaign is all about trying to help families who are in need find a safe and secure home before Christmas.

Mr Warren, alongside mental health advocate Adam Mumford, originally called on the ACT government to identify and approve 20 suitable vacant properties for renovation by a collection of tradespeople and businesses.

As it stands, there are more than 580 public housing properties currently vacant across the ACT.

The breakthrough instead has come from the private sector, a local client and friend offering a home for the project.

The private owner is offering a four-bed and two-bath residency to the 20 Homes campaign for six to nine months at a reduced rate of rent.

"It would normally rent for $850 to $900 [a week], but he has offered it to us at $400," Mr Mumford said.

Mr Warren, who was homeless as a young man, was thrilled the campaign had secured its first property.

"This is the moment we've been working towards. Our first home is real," he said. "A generous client and friend has made this possible, and I'm forever grateful.

"Now we need the community to help us turn this house into a home. This is what making a difference feels like."

But the hard work is far from done even at the site of this property.

Before it can welcome a family, fresh carpet, curtains and a paint job are needed, as are volunteers to help clean, apply said paint and lay the carpet.

The campaign is calling on Canberra residents, businesses and tradespeople to contribute materials, time or skills.

The goal is to have the home ready by December 14.

Work is also continuing on the government commitment to roll out 20 homes.

"This is a real first step, and there is more work ahead. We're asking Canberra to come together and help us get this home ready," Mr Warren said.

The campaign welcomes donations of carpet, curtains and paint, along with volunteers who can help with cleaning, painting and carpet installation.
